title: Islanded GPU farms: per-tenant throughput contracts, adaptive eviction & autoscale shaping
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem statement: customers on Dedicated capacity require hard per-tenant throughput guarantees while co-located workloads cause noisy-neighbor tail latency spikes and opaque cost regression. Current soft-slicing + basic token-bucket enforcement is sufficient for best-effort fairness but fails to preserve SLOs under bursty, long-tail workloads and mixed precision kernels.

Goal: Implement an "islanded GPU farms" model that combines fast-path soft isolation with optional hard partitioning signals, a lease-backed throughput contract, and an adaptive eviction strategy that prioritizes SLO preservation and graceful degradation. The implementation should integrate with the autoscaler so that tenants with active contracts receive proactive capacity expansion and those without contracts are subject to progressive throttling/eviction.

Scope: backend scheduler changes (cgroup/qos integration), runtime telemetry hooks (per-tenant tail-latency histograms and kernel contention metrics), autoscaler policy extension (shape-aware demand predictor + contract-aware scaling), and rollout of operator controls in the Console (per-tenant contract view and manual quarantine). Prototype to be validated on a 24-node staging pool with mixed A100/H100 shapes and 3 synthetic noisy workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant lease API to request and commit throughput contracts (tokens/sec and burst allowance) implemented and surfaced in Dedicated control plane
Scheduler enforces a two-tier isolation model: soft lane enforcement (token buckets + KV-cache affinity) and hard island signal (node pinning) when contract is taken
Adaptive eviction algorithm implemented: fairness scoring + tail-latency penalty leads to deterministic eviction ordering and avoids oscillation for 95th/99th percentile SLOs
Autoscaler respects contracts: proactive scale-up within contractual SLA window and graceful scale-down with traffic draining
End-to-end test: a tenant with a throughput contract maintains <150ms p95 under a synthetic noisy neighbor that increases request rate 3x for 10 minutes
Console additions: per-tenant contract dashboard, manual quarantine button, and audit log link
Documentation: PRD + ops runbook and upgrade notes published to Confluence and linked in ticket
notes: Decision log 2026-02-18: use lease-backed token contract rather than pre-reserved hard slices by default to retain cluster utilization for bursty tenants

Trade-off: hard node pinning reduces noisy neighbor risk but increases cold-start frequency for fractional tenants; we add a hybrid signal so small contracts use soft lanes and large contracts can opt into pinning
Telemetry: added per-tenant kernel contention metric via eBPF prototype (see PR) to better predict eviction impact
Fallback policy: if autoscaler misses, runtime will shift tenant to a compatible quantized model variant before eviction
